To the Honorable John G. Roberts, Jr., Chief Justice of the United States and 

Circuit Justice for the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia 

Circuit: 

For the reasons stated below, Respondents Committee on Oversight and 

Reform, Committee on Financial Services, and Permanent Select Committee on 

Intelligence of the U.S. House of Representatives respectfully request leave to file a 

brief on the merits in excess of the word limit set forth in Supreme Court Rule 

33.1(g)(vi), not to exceed 17,000 words. 

1. 

On December 13, 2019, this Court granted the petition for a writ of 

certiorari in Donald J. Trump, et al., v. Mazars USA, LLP, et al. (No. 19-715).  The 

Court treated the application for stay in Donald J. Trump, et al. v. Deutsche Bank 

AG, et al. (No. 19-760) as a certiorari petition, granted certiorari, and consolidated 

the two cases. 

2. 

On January 7, 2020, Petitioners applied to file a consolidated brief on 

the merits in excess of the word limits set forth in Rules 33.1(g)(v) and (vii).  

Petitioners sought 19,000 words for their principal brief and 9,000 words for their 

reply brief.  The Committees agreed that consolidated briefing was appropriate but 

took the position that Petitioners’ briefs should not exceed 15,000 and 7,000 words, 

respectively.  Respondents Mazars USA, LLP, Deutsche Bank AG, and Capital One 

Financial Corporation took no position on the application.  

1

3. 

On January 13, 2020, Petitioners’ application was granted in part.  

Petitioners were permitted to file a principal brief no longer than 17,000 words and 

a reply brief no longer than 8,000 words. 

4. 

5. 

The Committees intend to file a single brief on the merits. 

The consolidated cases involve separate investigations by three 

committees of the United States House of Representatives, each furthering distinct 

legislative and oversight purposes.  So that they may adequately present their cases 

(and in light of the length of Petitioners’ briefs), the Committees respectfully 

request leave to file a brief on the merits in excess of the 13,000-word limit imposed 

by Rule 33.1(g)(vi), not to exceed 17,000 words, the same limit now applicable to 

Petitioners’ opening brief. 

6. 

Counsel for the Committees has conferred with counsel for Petitioners, 

who stated that Petitioners consent to this request.  Respondent Deutsche Bank AG 

has stated that it takes no position on this application.  Respondents Mazars USA, 

LLP and Capital One Financial Corporation have stated that they do not object. 

2
